fields.description:
## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` is 798 LOC (2 under the 800 cap) and a "god command": it
bundles the compaction **transaction** (`_compact_locked`, CCN 24), **snapshot
reconstruction** (`rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`, CCN 21), and the **CLI** surface in one
file. Zero in-progress contention. Flagged by audit ae1b for both size and complexity. It
also blocks bug `aea0`, whose one-line fix plus its rationale comment does not fit.

## Approach
Turn `compact.py` into a thin CLI facade over two extracted engines, decomposed by
responsibility (the recurrence-preventing fix — future mechanism/format changes land in the
engine module, not the command file). The public CLI entry points **stay in `compact.py`**
so the contended `_cli/__init__.py` dispatcher is NOT touched.

1. **`compact_txn.py`** (NEW) — the compaction TRANSACTION: `_compact_locked`,
   `_sync_before_compact`, `_maybe_pause_at_rename_barrier`, `_git`, **and the snapshot
   primitives BOTH engines share**: `_git_author`, `_snapshot_strip_keys`,
   `_build_authorship_ledger`.
2. **`compact_rebuild.py`** (NEW) — snapshot reconstruction: `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`,
   `_read_event_uuid`, and the rebuild counter. **Move the counter with its incrementer:**
   `_REBUILD_COUNT` and `get_rebuild_count` MUST live here, because
   `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` does `global _REBUILD_COUNT` — leaving `get_rebuild_count`
   in `compact.py` would read a different module global and silently report zero.
   `get_rebuild_count` is re-exported from `compact.py` to preserve its path.
3. `compact.py` retains the CLI facade: `compact_cli`, `compact_all_cli`,
   `_scan_snapshot_state`, `_usage`, plus the re-exports.

### Why the shared helpers live in `compact_txn`, not `compact_rebuild`
The dependency MUST run one way. `_compact_locked` needs `_build_authorship_ledger`,
`_snapshot_strip_keys` and `_git_author`; `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` needs those SAME
three plus `_git`. Splitting them — helpers in `compact_rebuild`, `_git` in `compact_txn` —
makes each module import the other, i.e. a circular import. Hosting all four in
`compact_txn` gives `compact -> {txn, rebuild}` and `rebuild -> txn`, which is acyclic, and
puts the repair path in the natural position of depending on the normal path.

Complexity reduction rides on the move: `_compact_locked` gives up its candidate-parse,
snapshot-envelope, retire/rollback and commit clusters to named helpers, and the rebuild
gives up its source-partition and commit clusters. Update `.github/complexity-baseline.json`
**downward only** (shrink-only ratchet).

Rationale (G6): the three responsibilities have different change-drivers (transaction
safety, snapshot format, CLI ergonomics); separating them gives each a stable home.

## Preserve public + test import paths via re-export (G1G2)
Every consumer outside this module reaches the moved symbols through
`rebar._commands.compact`, so `compact.py` must re-export them. The VERIFIED consumer set
(semantic search + string grep, per AGENTS.md — the string grep matters because two sites
name the symbol as a monkeypatch STRING):

- `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` — `_commands/fsck_repair.py:269` and
  `_commands/fsck_restore.py:202`, both importing INSIDE the function body (so the attribute
  is re-read per call and the string monkeypatch below still lands). Tests:
  `tests/integration/test_b636_rebuild_history_loss.py:78,138`,
  `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py:946`,
  `tests/unit/test_identity_4e9d_heldout.py:123` (via `_compact.`), and monkeypatched BY
  STRING at `tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_stale_channel_repair.py:46` and
  `test_fsck_stale_channel_repair_heldout.py:97,131,189,229`.
  **NOT** imported by `_commands/fsck.py` — fsck.py:281 only MENTIONS the name in a comment.
- `_snapshot_strip_keys` — `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:9`,
  `tests/unit/test_legacy_signature_mirror_drop.py:14`, and
  `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_creation_channel_compaction.py:138` (via `_compact.`).
- `_build_authorship_ledger` — `tests/unit/test_identity_gate_scope_and_ledger.py:362,401`
  and `tests/unit/test_authorship_batched_ticket_map_7084.py:176,215,238,244`.
- `get_rebuild_count` — no consumer outside `compact.py` was found; re-exported anyway to
  keep the documented path stable.

  Also `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_creation_channel_compaction.py:170` calls
  `_compact.rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` — re-export-covered, no edit needed.

These are plain `from ... import` / attribute consumers, so the re-exports keep them passing
with NO edit.

## `compact.py` also needs these symbols for ITSELF — not only as re-exports
Distinct from the public re-export list above: the functions that STAY in `compact.py`
consume three symbols this split moves out, so the facade must bind them back or it will
not even import.

- `compact_cli` calls `_sync_before_compact` and `_compact_locked`.
- `compact_all_cli`'s batch-commit block (`compact.py:778-782` pre-split) calls `_git`.

So `compact.py` does `from .compact_txn import _compact_locked, _git, _sync_before_compact`
in addition to the re-exported names. `_git` is therefore bound for BOTH reasons — the
facade's own use and the module-attribute seam a test patches — which is why it is listed
twice and must not be pruned as "unused" by a lint pass.

## Two test seams MUST be repointed — the monkeypatch hazard
`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_negative.py` patches implementation internals ON
THE `compact` MODULE OBJECT, and those internals move:

- `monkeypatch.setattr(_compact, "_git", ...)` — `_compact_locked` reads `compact_txn`'s
  module global, so a patch on the facade does not take. This does not merely fail loudly:
  the compaction SUCCEEDS, the test's `assert rc == 1` fails, and had the assertion been
  weaker the test would have passed while exercising nothing.
- `monkeypatch.setattr(_compact.lock, "acquire", ...)` — `compact.py` no longer imports
  `lock`, so the attribute does not exist (AttributeError).

Both are repointed at the symbol's new home (`compact_txn._git`; `_lock`, which the file
already imports). This is the ONLY test change, it is mechanical, and it is REQUIRED — the
earlier "no test edits" claim was wrong and is corrected here. Both failures were confirmed
empirically by running the suite against the split before touching the tests.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` — CLI facade + re-exports.
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py` — NEW (transaction + shared snapshot primitives).
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_rebuild.py` — NEW (snapshot reconstruction).
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` — shrink-only.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_negative.py` — repoint the two seams above.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_rebuild_counter_b2bb.py` — NEW: the
  counter-increment proof (it needs the `rebar_repo` fixture, which is scoped to
  `tests/interfaces/`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `wc -l src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` <= 500; both new modules >= 100 LOC; the
      module-size gate is green. MEASURED on the merged change: compact.py 275,
      compact_txn.py 448, compact_rebuild.py 238; `test_module_size_contract.py` passes.
- [x] `.github/complexity-baseline.json` entries for `_compact_locked` and
      `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` are <= their current values (24 / 21) or removed
      entirely, and `check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports `new=0 increased=0`.
      ALL THREE compact.py entries were REMOVED (decomposition put every function under the
      reporting threshold) — a pure shrink, which the locked ratchet accepts. `--check` now
      reports `active=65 new=0 increased=0 stale=0` and zero `compact.py::` entries remain.
- [x] `_cli/__init__.py` is unchanged (`git diff --name-only <commit>~1 <commit> --
      src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` returns nothing), and
      `python -c "import rebar._commands.compact as c; c.rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log;
      c.compact_cli; c.compact_all_cli; c._snapshot_strip_keys; c._build_authorship_ledger;
      c.get_rebuild_count"` resolves all six names.
- [x] The counter co-location is PROVEN, not merely re-exported: a test calls
      `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` on a real ticket and asserts
      `compact.get_rebuild_count()` strictly increased across the call. Without this the
      suite could stay green while `get_rebuild_count` read a different module global and
      silently reported zero — the exact failure the co-location exists to prevent. (No
      consumer outside `compact.py` exercises the counter today, so nothing else covers it.)
- [x] Full default suite green — 11820 passed, 155 skipped. The only EDIT to an existing test
      is repointing the two monkeypatch seams in `test_compact_negative.py` (no assertion
      weakened); the other test file touched is the NEW counter proof, an addition.
